# ui::VisualTree

Header: `winui/ui/VisualTree.hpp`.

A flat, data-oriented snapshot of the laid-out tree's shape: one slot per [Element](element.md), with parent / first-child / next-sibling links by stable [VisualId](../core/namespace-ui.md#visualid), bounds and dirty flags held in parallel arrays.

[Window::layout()](window.md#layout) clears and rebuilds it on every pass that re-lays out, through [Element::build_visual_tree()](element.md#build_visual_tree), and hands it out read-only via [Window::visual_tree()](window.md#visual_tree). It is an inspection surface (tests, tooling), not a way to drive controls: changes go through the [Element](element.md) tree. Slots are indices in pre-order and are only valid until the next rebuild; a [VisualId](../core/namespace-ui.md#visualid) stays the same across rebuilds.

Example: 
```cpp
// Every element of a laid-out window, flat, for a tool that inspects the tree:
const ui::VisualTree& tree = window.visual_tree();
for (std::size_t slot = 0; slot < tree.size(); ++slot)
{
    const ui::Rect& bounds = tree.bounds_at(slot);
    std::println("{} under {}: {}x{}", tree.id_at(slot), tree.parent_at(slot), bounds.width, bounds.height);
}

// And one element by its id, here a button built with `.control = save_button`:
ui::Control<ui::Button> save_button;
std::size_t             slot = 0;
if (save_button && tree.find(save_button->visual_id(), slot))
{
    std::println("Save is at {}, {}", tree.bounds_at(slot).x, tree.bounds_at(slot).y);
}
```

## clear

```cpp
void clear()
```

Drops every node; the tree is empty ([size()](#size) == 0) afterwards.

## add_node

```cpp
std::size_t add_node(VisualId id, VisualId parent, const Rect& bounds, DirtyFlags flags_at_build = DirtyFlags::None)
```

Append a node under `parent` (InvalidVisualId for the root) and return its slot. `id` must be unique within the tree and, if `parent` is not InvalidVisualId, `parent` must already be in the tree (asserted). Nodes are expected in pre-order (parent before children), which is how [Element::build_visual_tree](element.md#build_visual_tree) walks the logical tree; a new child becomes the last in its parent's sibling chain. `bounds` is in window DIPs and `flags_at_build` records what was still dirty when the snapshot was taken.

## size

```cpp
std::size_t size() const
```

The number of nodes; valid slots are [`0 .. size() - 1`](#size), in insertion (pre-)order.

## id_at

```cpp
VisualId id_at(std::size_t slot) const
```

The stable [VisualId](../core/namespace-ui.md#visualid) of the node in `slot`. The `*_at()` accessors do not bounds-check.

## parent_at

```cpp
VisualId parent_at(std::size_t slot) const
```

The parent's id, or InvalidVisualId for the root.

## first_child_at

```cpp
VisualId first_child_at(std::size_t slot) const
```

The first child's id, or InvalidVisualId for a leaf.

## next_sibling_at

```cpp
VisualId next_sibling_at(std::size_t slot) const
```

The next child of the same parent, in add order, or InvalidVisualId for the last one.

## bounds_at

```cpp
const Rect& bounds_at(std::size_t slot) const
```

The node's arranged bounds at snapshot time, in window DIPs.

## flags_at

```cpp
DirtyFlags flags_at(std::size_t slot) const
```

The node's dirty flags at snapshot time ([Window::layout()](window.md#layout) builds before clearing them).

## find

```cpp
bool find(VisualId id, std::size_t& out_slot) const
```

Look up a node's slot by its stable id in O(1). Returns false, leaving `out_slot` untouched, when no node has that id.
